subject: Accounting for low detection with occuMulti

messages.author: 7347479aef4e9693
messages.subject: Accounting for low detection with occuMulti
parts:
Hello again, everyone!

I’m using the occuMulti function to assess single-season occupancy and co-occurrence of four rodent species across the Bay Area. My data are structured as a list of imputed datasets with four rows for each of 76 sites (one per species), columns for each site- and/or species-specific independent variable (e.g., Area, Dist_urban, Above_MHW, Connectivity, Effort, and Year), and columns for detection/non-detection data for each species across sampling events.

When fitting the null model, the detection probabilities for each species are quite low (0.38, 0.27, 0.38, and 0.09). From my understanding of MSOMs, low detection values can cause issues, such as poor occupancy and species interaction estimates. I attempted to incorporate detection-level covariates (Effort and Year), but this didn’t yield better results, with the top model ~Effort + Year producing weighted detection probabilities of 0.24, 0.28, 0.81, and 0.11, respectively.

I also tried restructuring the detection/non-detection data for a removal model, but this didn’t work due to mismatched numbers of missing observations across species. Unfortunately, I can’t return to the field and do not have additional detection-level covariates to assess.

Does anyone have suggestions for how to proceed with low detection probabilities or approaches I might have missed?

Thanks in advance!

Thanks,
Kristin

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Accounting for low detection with occuMulti
parts:
hi Kristin, 
 I don't have a lot of experience with these models myself but I think the only thing you can really do in this lowish-p situation is to have more sites.  I think the limitation here is the number of sites, not so much the realized values of p. 
 I can't remember if this paper was sent around recently but it might be worth looking at:
Cowans, A., Bonet Bigata, A. and Sutherland, C., 2024. Sample size considerations for species co-occurrence models. bioRxiv, pp.2024-09.
Sample size considerations for species co-occurrence models | bioRxiv
regards
andy

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Accounting for low detection with occuMulti
parts:
hi Kristin,
 unfortunately I can't make a recommendation about this, I just don't have enough experience with these models. In general I would say that if you leave out an important species that interacts with other species, you will be misled potentially quite severely with regard to the interaction of other species.  This is actually an interesting question, and I think it relates to a lot of concepts in Causal Inference (also outside of my area of expertise!). I hope others on the list can say something about this.
regards
andy
